definitions: To enter a building or place illegally, typically by force.
To train a new horse or to wear new shoes until they are comfortable.
To make something, especially a new piece of equipment, ready for use by using it gently at first.
examples: Someone tried to break into the house last night.
Please don't break in while I'm speaking.
It took a while to break in the new boots.
You need to break in a new engine carefully.
